clauses.clause: sec. 1: amends EO 10575 (foreign-aid delegations) in paragraphs (a)-(z-2), including new secs. 108, 109 and 302
sec. 2, first sentence: revokes Part II of EO 10610
sec. 2, second sentence: other inconsistent provisions of EO 10610 are subject to the amendments of EO 10575
sec. 3: amends first sentence of sec. 2(a) of EO 10477 to add the Secretary of State's authority under sec. 571 of the Foreign Service Act

conclusion.basis_rule: mixed: (a) express named supersession for secs. 1-2; (c) spent on issue for sec. 2 first sentence; (d) amendment-only follows parent for sec. 3
conclusion.formal_status: partly_superseded: secs. 1 and 2 expressly superseded by name (EO 10893 sec. 305(a)(6)); sec. 3 never expressly revoked or superseded by name, its effect ended when its parent provision (EO 10477 sec. 2) was revoked by EO 12292 sec. 10(f)

moves.note: Operative status NO by three routes: sec. 2 first sentence spent on issue (1959-05-20); secs. 1-2 superseded by name by EO 10893 sec. 305(a)(6) (1960-11-08); sec. 3 is amendment-only and follows its parent, EO 10477 sec. 2, which EO 12292 sec. 10(f) revoked effective 1981-02-15. Formal status is partial: EO 12292 names EO 10477 sec. 2, not EO 10822 sec. 3, so sec. 3 was never itself expressly revoked or superseded.
All four clauses have an end date and a quoted source.

No open gap; every ending proposition was upheld on review and the conclusion is repackaged as the reviewer required. Caveats: originals read from held OCR text of the official FR PDFs, not the page images; p11 (counterevidence only) was read from the eCFR versioner API for 2026-10-14 through a web-fetch summary that returned the authority line in segments. The independent review supported T4 before these repairs.

review.conclusion_reason: NO operative status is upheld: sections 1-2 were expressly superseded on November 8, 1960; section 2's revocation was already spent on issue; section 3 follows its parent provision, revoked effective February 15, 1981. However, the conclusion as packaged conflates these routes with complete express named ending of EO 10822. Formal status should specify partial express supersession, with section 3's effect ended through revocation of its parent provision. February 15, 1981 is the final operative ending, not the first clause ending.
review.suspected_defect: Possible conflation of operative exhaustion with full formal revocation or supersession: EO 12292 names EO 10477 section 2, not EO 10822 section 3. No clearly fabricated quotation was found.

verdicts.reason: Held FR text identifies EO 10822 at 24 FR 4159 and ends with the signature date May 20, 1959.
Held section 1 introduces amendments solely to EO 10575; the other orders are identified as previous amendments or effects.
Held section 2 states that Part II of EO 10610 'is hereby revoked,' supporting spent-on-issue treatment.
Held section 3 expressly adds wording to the first sentence of EO 10477 section 2(a).
Held EO 10893 section 305(a) supersedes the listed orders and parts. Despite damaged OCR, item (6) retains '1 and 2' and EO 10822's number and date; the cited APP text confirms the complete wording.

Held EO 10893 section 305(a)(1)-(2) expressly lists EO 10575 and EO 10610 under 'are hereby superseded.' Section 305(b) preserves section 301 arrangements, qualifying the consequences but not the quoted supersession.
Held EO 12292 section 10(f) expressly revokes 'Section 2 of Executive Order No. 10477 of August 1,1953.'
Held EO 12292 section 11 states: 'This Order shall be effective as of February 15,1981.'
The opened https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/22/1472 prints section 2 as revoked by EO 12292 and omits the section 571 language.
The opened https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/22/1472 names EO 10822 in EO 10477's amendment history; the affected section 2 is expressly marked revoked.
The cited cutoff-date eCFR URL failed to load on two attempts. The evidence-slice snippet is only a lead and cannot independently verify the proposition.
